assembly.trim: onset: walk back from the peak above -36 dB re word peak tolerating <= 40 ms gaps (keeps the audible /b/ voice bar), 20 ms pre; offset -26 dB, 30 ms post, 6 ms fade-in, 20 ms fade-out; 70 Hz high-pass
assembly.loudness: RMS of frames above 25% of the word's peak matched to 0.085 (full scale); poem peak <= 0.89

audio.timing_method: measured: word onsets/offsets are the sample positions of each trimmed take in the assembly; syllable boundaries inside binturong/popcorn/never are the deepest 10 ms RMS-envelope minima between voiced humps; nucleus = frames above 45% of the syllable's peak. Checked against voice_poem_waveform.png (structurally verified). Listening check: NOT performed by this unit (no audio playback here) - perceptual check pending for the editor/critic.

visemes.jaw_rule: jaw = openness(shape) x (0.65 + 0.35 x rms_rel); rms_rel = syllable RMS peak / loudest syllable in the poem (linguistic shape separated from measured emphasis, SCION #47 sec. 6), so '-rong' (A) opens widest although 'bin' is louder. MBP onsets are keyed 50 ms before the measured burst (lip closure is silent). Recommended picture lead: 1 frame (42 ms) before the audio key.

responses.speaker: Reader A (fictional)
responses.quoted_span: A gong? Something you strike — bin, tu, RONG.
responses.hypothesis: The name is an onomatopoeia: a struck metal object (a gong) whose 'RONG' is its ring.
responses.next_observation: Seeing the words spelled should test whether it is a thing that is struck or a name; a verb like 'rings' in the text would confirm, 'never rings' would contradict.

responses.speaker: Reader B (fictional)
responses.quoted_span: It hangs and swings… a lantern? A bell that's gone quiet?
responses.hypothesis: Something suspended that sways but makes no sound: a lantern, or a bell that 'never rings'.
responses.next_observation: A picture of the thing on the cord would test whether it is an object at all; 'smells of popcorn' does not yet fit a lantern.

responses.speaker: Reader A (fictional)
responses.quoted_span: Oh — it hangs by its tail. 'Never rings': it was never a gong.
responses.hypothesis: A binturong is an animal that hangs by its tail; 'never rings' now reads literally as a denial of the gong guess. Shift caused by the image (the tail on the knot), checked against the text.
responses.next_observation: Hearing L1 again should test whether 'hangs' and 'swings' now read as the animal's own movement; the popcorn smell is unverified by the picture.

responses.speaker: Reader B (fictional)
responses.quoted_span: Maybe. It still swings like a lantern — I'd want to see it move.
responses.hypothesis: Accepts the animal provisionally but keeps the lantern reading alive: the engraving is a still, so 'swings' is not yet shown.
responses.next_observation: Moving footage of a binturong (not released in this film) would decide whether it swings; the reading stays open.
